tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Get exact service.version, identity, default tenant, supported capabilities and every visible tenant's used/limit/remaining quota in one call. Eligible tenants register automatically. No quota_get or deployment previews needed for this overview.

tools.name: quota_get
tools.description: Refresh one tenant's used/limit/remaining quota; whoami already includes all visible tenants.

tools.name: catalog_get
tools.description: Use this for questions about Carrel features, images or the development environment. Get exact service.version, installed images, size presets, VM/CT restrictions, MiB/GiB units and supported capabilities together. No deployment preview needed to discover support. Images include environment, default_size and default_swap_mb; minimal and development are distinct prepared images.

tools.name: capacity_get
tools.description: Get live aggregate physical CPU/RAM/storage, admission headroom and policy. Shared capacity is separate from tenant quota; no other tenants' guest details. GPU allocation is unsupported, GPU hardware inventory unknown.

tools.name: machine_create
tools.description: Create one VM/CT directly when the user asks for a machine. Defaults: Debian 13 minimal VM, 1 vCPU, 1 GiB RAM, 10 GiB disk, 1 GiB swap. Supply an SSH public key inline or use saved keys. No discovery or preview call is required; admission checks run during creation. Waits up to 55 seconds and returns verified readiness and SSH details in operation.result; only call operation_get if still pending. dry_run=true is optional for preview requests. Use VMs for Docker, OVS, Mininet or databases. CTs do not support packages, runcmd, health_checks or nested_virt. Use deployment_apply for multiple machines, connections or publications. Use the known default public key only if saved keys are unavailable; do not scan unrelated SSH configuration. Successful summary omits quota tables; detail=full retrieves them. For local CLI clients, creation includes merging returned ssh_config while preserving existing entries, verifying its tenant-qualified alias with ssh -G, and presenting ssh_short. Use direct ssh only if client setup is unavailable, excluded or fails. Minimal has no Node, Docker or compilers. Choose image=debian-13 or ubuntu-24.04 for prepared development tools and default size=small (2 vCPU/2 GiB/20 GiB). Explicit size/resource fields override image defaults. CTs default to tiny with no swap. Choose larger resources for builds and Docker stacks.

image.description: Default VM: debian-13-minimal. Debian/Ubuntu development images remain available. CTs use debian-13 or ubuntu-24.04. Or "tenant:<name>" for one of this tenant's imported cloud images (image_import); the disk is at least the image's virtual size.

size.description: Defaults to tiny for minimal VMs/CTs, small for development VMs. Explicit resource fields override this preset.

network_access.description: tenant allows all same-tenant primary traffic. restricted permits SSH/publications and declared connections only; choose restricted for app/database isolation. It filters the primary NIC only; private experiment NICs stay unfiltered.

swap_mb.description: Swap in MiB, within the virtual disk. Default 1024 for VMs, 0 for CTs; set 0 to disable.

health_checks.description: Optional checks after cloud-init. Examples: {"type":"http","port":80,"path":"/","status":200}, {"type":"tcp","port":5432}, {"type":"service","service":"nginx"}. HTTP/TCP always target 127.0.0.1; specify port, not a URL. No checks means application readiness is not verified.

runcmd.description: VM bootstrap commands as argument arrays. Each argument is limited to 65536 UTF-8 bytes; the complete MCP HTTP request is limited to 256 KiB. Use scp/rsync over SSH after creation for larger project files.

idempotency_key.description: Stable unique key for retrying a background submission after a lost response; reuse only with identical arguments.

public_ssh.description: false: no public SSH port; the machine is reached through the site's SSH jump host (ssh -J jump@<origin>), so it uses none of the tenant's 10 public ports. The returned ssh_config sets ProxyJump.

iso.description: Install from one of this tenant's ISOs (iso_import) instead of an image: an empty disk with the ISO attached, no cloud-init, no SSH keys. The machine stays installing until machine_media ejects the ISO; machine_get shows the address, gateway and DNS to type into the installer (no DHCP). Default size small.

firmware.description: With iso: the firmware the installer expects.

tpm.description: With iso and firmware uefi: a TPM 2.0, for systems such as Windows 11.

user_data.description: Only for an image imported with ports: the document passed unchanged as cloud-init user-data, such as a Talos machine config. Omitted, a Talos VM boots into maintenance mode for talosctl apply-config --insecure. Stored like a secret: never shown or audited.

tools.name: domain_add
tools.description: Publish HTTPS at <sub>.<tenant>.winlab.tw, or with name at a special domain the tenant was granted (domain_request): the granted name, or for a wildcard grant the catch-all *.<base> or one label under it. Give exactly one of sub and name. Under an srv grant, domain_add writes an SRV record that names carrel.winlab.tw and the public port that forwards to the machine's target_port with the grant's protocol; open that port with port_open first. DNS and TLS are automatic; the operation waits until routing is configured. Application responses require an external check. sub "*" is a catch-all: every single-label name under the tenant without its own domain goes to that target, for an ingress controller that routes by Host. The gateway ends TLS and forwards plain HTTP with the original Host header, X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto; WebSockets pass through. With vip instead of machine, the gateway forwards to the virtual address.

tools.name: vpn_client_add
tools.description: Connect a device or an agent to the tenant's network over WireGuard, for traffic SSH port forwarding does not cover: UDP, many ports, a browser on internal services. Generate the key pair on the client (wg genkey | tee key | wg pubkey) and send only the public key; carrel never sees the private key. The result's config is a WireGuard configuration: put the private key in it, then bring it up with wg-quick (needs root) or, without root, a userspace client such as wireproxy (WireGuard as a local SOCKS5 proxy). The client gets an address in 10.201.N.0/24 and reaches the tenant's machines with network_access tenant, nothing else. It expires after hours (default 8, at most 168); adding the same name again renews it. One TCP port is simpler with the SSH jump host (ssh -L). At most 8 clients per tenant.

instructions:
WinLab machines through MCP. For feature questions use catalog_get. If tool discovery is needed, list names first and inspect only relevant definitions; do not dump all descriptions or repeated instructions. Ordinary member tasks use these tools directly, without operator memories, infrastructure runbooks, hypervisor access or unrelated SSH inspection. Use the known machine name; machine_list only when asked to list or when the target is ambiguous. Omit tenant for personal resources. No discovery or preview is required for an authorized action.
Create -> machine_create; status/connect -> machine_get; start/shutdown/reboot/pause/resume -> machine_power; resize -> machine_resize; delete -> machine_delete; disk snapshots -> snapshot_*; HTTPS -> domain_add; a name outside *.<tenant>.winlab.tw -> domain_request, then domain_add with name once approved; TCP/UDP -> port_open; a fixed public port such as 25565 -> port_request, then port_open with public_port once approved. Deploy on every push -> app_link (then run its install line over SSH and commit its workflow); status -> app_get. shutdown is graceful; stop is forced and requires explicit intent. VM pause retains RAM, disks and quota; CT pause is unsupported. Deletion is never a substitute for shutdown. Required confirmation fields express the user's existing authorization; ask only when intent/target is unclear. Do not shut down running work just to resize without authorization.
Creation defaults: Debian 13 minimal VM, 1 vCPU, 1 GiB RAM, 10 GiB disk, 1 GiB swap. The default image debian-13-minimal has SSH, cloud-init, Python for management, security updates and basic transfer tools; Node, Docker and compilers are not preinstalled. For a prepared development VM choose image=debian-13 or ubuntu-24.04 (default size=small: 2 vCPU/2 GiB/20 GiB). size=tiny is 1 vCPU/1 GiB/10 GiB; individual cpu, memory_mb and disk_gb override the preset. New CTs default to Debian 13 with tiny and no swap. Choose larger resources for builds, Docker stacks and databases as needed. Prefer known saved public keys; otherwise read only the known default public key and pass it inline. ssh_key_add saves it once for future creation. Inline keys are not auto-saved. Never read/send private keys or tokens in tool arguments. VMs support Docker and cloud-init; CTs do not support packages/runcmd/health_checks/nested_virt.
Member mutations wait up to 55 seconds. Inspect operation.state/result/error; succeeded needs no follow-up poll/list/quota just to prove the requested platform action. Offline NIC configuration can still await start/resume; resize can require owner filesystem work. Follow explicit result requirements. Pending: follow next_action and poll_after_seconds with operation_get. wait_seconds=0 submits immediately. Queued is not reserved or completed; disconnects do not cancel jobs. Reuse an idempotency_key for an identical lost submission. operation_retry resumes; revise_request requires corrected arguments. Summary is default; detail=full retains full accounting/identifiers. Errors and previews keep diagnostics.
Preview only when asked to plan/compare. deployment_plan is the complete preview. Authorized groups use deployment_apply directly with machines, connections and publications. restricted permits declared connections/public services; tenant allows same-tenant traffic. Use access=[{machine, network_access, confirm: machine_name}] with deployment_apply to change existing ingress together with connections; previews explain connectivity changes. SSH, publications and old explicit peer grants are preserved. Extra networks/NICs are advanced experiments. No host/bridge/VLAN/gateway choices are needed.
For local CLI clients, completing a creation or connection request includes SSH alias setup by default: merge returned ssh_config into the connecting client config, preserve existing entries, verify the returned tenant-qualified alias HostName/User/Port with ssh -G, then present ssh_short as the primary command. Do not wait for a separate alias request. Status-only requests need no local edits. If local file access is unavailable, the user excludes setup, or setup fails, present ssh and explain that the alias is not installed. Aliases are client config, not DNS; name reuse may change port/host identity. Do not disable host-key checking or replace unrelated aliases.
whoami: identity/version/all quotas; catalog_get: images/environment/sizes; quota_get: one quota; capacity_get: shared capacity. These are not prerequisites. machine_list state is recorded; machine_get power and SSH are live; guest report freshness is independent. Unknown/stale readiness is not an application health claim. Readiness includes SSH, initialization and requested application checks; not_checked and publication routing_configured do not verify an application response. MiB: memory_mb/swap_mb; GiB: disk_gb. Previews reserve/mutate nothing, record audit and retain requirements/quota changes. Membership is checked each request. Tools only, no MCP resources.
Default personal/project quota: 8 machines and 8 IPs, 8 vCPU, 16 GiB RAM, 100 GiB disk; totals still apply. Each SSH uses one of 10 tenant public ports, leaving two for extra TCP/UDP publications when eight machines exist. HTTPS domains do not consume these ports. Stopped/paused machines retain reservations. Resize needs available quota and node capacity; disk only grows and owner SSH must verify/grow the filesystem.
